request: How is the Highway Trust Fund financed, and when is it projected to run short of money?
escalation_reason: The quick pass answered only part of the question.

reply.reply:
The Highway Trust Fund is funded primarily by motor-fuel taxes, but I can’t verify a projected shortfall date from the checked passages. Fuel taxes supplied 82% of Trust Fund revenue in FY2015–FY2024, including 58% from the federal gas tax alone (CRS R48948, PDF p. 3). Of the 18.4-cent federal gasoline tax, 18.3 cents goes to the Trust Fund (CRS R48948, PDF p. 4); Congress has also used Treasury general-fund transfers since 2008 to help keep it solvent (CRS R47573, PDF p. 2). CRS reports a conditional CBO projection of the Highway Account approaching zero in FY2028, but that finding did not pass independent verification, so treat the date as unconfirmed here.

[See the brief for details](output/briefs/case-20261025-153714-5420.html).
reply.reasoning: Verified findings support the financing explanation, but the latest FY2028 timing passage failed independent verification. I disclose it as unconfirmed rather than present it as an established projection.
